title: How to hide cursor in Safari on Mac: simple tricks and tools for clean screens
metaTitle: How to hide cursor in Safari on Mac: Simple Steps
description: Learn how to hide cursor on Mac while using Safari. Discover built-in tricks for video players and reliable third-party tools for a clean, distraction-free view.
targetKeyword: how to hide cursor on mac
intro: There is no native system-wide setting to hide the cursor on macOS. You can often hide it in Safari by moving your mouse to the edge of the screen during full-screen video playback.
tldr: Move your mouse to the screen edge to trigger auto-hide in video players.
Press the Escape key to force focus away from the cursor in full-screen mode.
Use third-party utilities like Cursorcerer for global cursor control.
Check your browser settings if specific sites force the cursor to remain visible.

stats.label: Native macOS settings for global cursor hiding

blocks.text: Why macOS lacks a native hide cursor setting

Apple designs macOS with a focus on accessibility and constant visibility. The cursor is a primary interaction tool. Because of this, the system does not include a simple checkbox to turn the pointer off. Most users only want to hide the cursor when they record their screen or watch a movie. In these cases, the system relies on individual apps to manage their own cursor behavior.

If you are struggling with a persistent cursor while watching videos in Safari, remember that the browser itself is often not the one controlling that visibility. The website code determines if the cursor should vanish. This is why you might see it disappear on YouTube but remain visible on other streaming platforms. When the website does not handle this, you need a different approach.
Using built-in tricks to hide the mouse cursor

Before you download extra software, try these manual methods. They work in many common scenarios without modifying your system files. First, enter full-screen mode in Safari. Move your mouse to the extreme right or bottom edge of your display. Many modern video players recognize this as a request to hide the interface, including the cursor. Wait a few seconds to see if it fades away.

Another trick involves the keyboard. When a video is playing, press the Escape key. This action sometimes tells the browser to relinquish focus from the cursor. It is not a permanent solution, but it often works for short intervals. If you need to keep the cursor hidden for longer, you might have to look at dedicated utilities.
Third-party tools for total cursor control

If you are a content creator or simply want a clean look, you need a tool that forces the cursor to hide. Cursorcerer is a popular choice for this. It adds a preference pane to your System Settings. You can set a global hotkey to toggle the cursor on or off at will. This works across every app, including Safari.

Another option is StealthPointer. This is a lightweight utility that lives in your menu bar. It offers similar features to Cursorcerer but with a different interface. It is useful if you want to create game profiles or specific rules for when the cursor should hide. Both tools use non-public APIs, which means they might stop working if Apple changes how the system handles pointers in a future macOS update.

Sometimes the cursor reappears even when you want it hidden. This usually happens because an app or website is programmatically demanding that the pointer be visible. Check if you have any browser extensions that might be interfering with your video player. Disabling them one by one can help you identify the culprit.

If you use a third-party tool, check for shortcut conflicts. If your hide-cursor hotkey is also used by another app, you might find that the cursor toggles at unexpected times. Open the settings for your utility and change the shortcut to a unique combination. This usually resolves most accidental visibility issues.

When you record your screen, the cursor can be a distraction. If you use a tool to hide it, remember to keep your keyboard shortcuts handy. You do not want to be stuck with an invisible cursor when you need to navigate to a new page. Always test your recording setup for a few seconds before you start the real session.

Ensure you download these utilities from trusted sources only. Because they interact with deep system settings, you should be careful about which apps you grant permissions to. Read the documentation provided by the developer on GitHub or their official website. Avoid sites that host suspicious installers.

faq.question: Can I hide the cursor in Safari without installing apps?
faq.answer: You can try moving the cursor to the edge of the screen or pressing the Escape key while in full-screen mode. These methods depend on the website's video player and are not always consistent.

faq.question: Does macOS have a setting to hide the mouse cursor?
faq.answer: No, macOS does not provide a native, user-accessible setting to force-hide the cursor system-wide.

faq.question: Why does my cursor keep appearing when I want it hidden?
faq.answer: The active application or website may be programmatically requesting that the cursor stay visible. Some apps are designed to force cursor visibility for better usability.

faq.question: Are third-party cursor tools safe?
faq.answer: Tools like Cursorcerer are widely used, but you should always download them from the official developer source to ensure they are safe and free from malware.

steps.name: Use full-screen mode
steps.text: Enter full-screen mode in Safari by clicking the green button in the top left of the window. Move your mouse to the far edge of the screen to trigger the player's native auto-hide function.

steps.name: Try the escape key
steps.text: If the cursor remains visible, press the Escape key on your keyboard. This sometimes forces the browser to drop focus from the pointer.

steps.name: Install a third-party tool
steps.text: If built-in methods fail, download a utility like Cursorcerer. Follow the instructions to add the preference pane to your System Settings.

steps.name: Toggle the cursor
steps.text: Use the designated hotkey, such as Option + Control + K, to toggle the cursor visibility on or off as needed.

troubleshooting.problem: The cursor will not hide even with a third-party tool.
troubleshooting.fix: The active website or app is likely forcing the cursor to be visible. Try a different browser or check for site-specific settings.

troubleshooting.problem: The hide cursor shortcut does not work.
troubleshooting.fix: Check System Settings to see if another app is using the same keyboard shortcut and reassign it if necessary.
